To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNA-binding proteins isolated from separate mouse cell clones grown under identical conditions differ with respect to molecular weight of the 0,15 M salt eluted protein.
the transcription of AKrJ DNA in vitro is inhibited by a 0.15 NaCl eluted DNA-binding protein from AKR mouse embryo cell cultures.

the DNA-binding proteins from separate clones of mouse embryo cells grown under the same conditions are not identical, that at least one protein is synthesized in different amounts, and that the 0.6 and 2.2 M NaCl eluants contain proteins which inhibit the transcription of mouse satellite DNA into RNA by E. coli polymerase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of the DNA-binding proteins of AKR mouse cells in culture and their possible involvement in the control of gene expression.
the characterization of proteins which may be involved in the control of DNA transcription in mouse cells in culture.
the characterization of proteins from mouse cells that are involved in the regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA-binding protein from mouse cells in tissue culture varies from clone to clone.
the DNA-binding proteins from AKR mouse cells are not identical.

the DNA-binding proteins from different mouse cell lines in culture have different properties and that these differences are reflected in differences in the transcription of the DNA of one clone compared to another.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transcription of DNA by E. coli and mammalian RNA polymerases is inhibited by the same proteins, and that the inhibition is due in part to competition between the DNA binding proteins and RNA polymerase for DNA binding sites.
the transcription of mouse DNA by RNA polymerase from E. coli is inhibited by DNA-binding proteins isolated from the mouse cells.
the DNA-binding proteins from separate clones of cells are different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA-binding proteins of the 0–6–2 M eluants from AKR mouse cells in culture are different.
the transcriptional machinery of mouse cells is complex and that the composition of the transcriptional machinery varies between clones.
the 0.6M NaCl eluate contains a DNA-binding protein that is present in all clones and that this protein can bind to the promoter region of the AKR gene.
